subject: occupancy model: does leaving out a latent variable (hierarchy level) result in an equivalent model?

messages.author: 39971e2c19b8ec70
messages.subject: occupancy model: does leaving out a latent variable (hierarchy level) result in an equivalent model?
parts:
Hello all!

Perhaps a trivial question, but I need to go back to basics :-) Sorry
if I missed it on Marc's trainings :-)

Say we have an occupancy model formulated as hierarchical bayesian model:

z[i] ~ dbern(pi[i])
logit(pi[i]) = .... # linear function of covariates for site i

y[i,j] ~ dbern(z[i] * p[i,j])

Because the only input data are the y[i,j] and we actually don't know
z[i] , I thought we could simplify (flatten) the model by removing the
latent variable z[] and having just:

y[i,j] ~ dbern(pi[i] * p[i,j])

The question is: Is this model equivalent to the first one?
y-prediction-wise, coefficient-wise, everything-wise (of course
everything except having z[] :-) If no, where is the difference?

I posted the question here with more detail, feel free to respond
there if you like https://stats.stackexchange.com/q/441829/5509

My thoughts are:

- maybe it should be equivalent, because z[] is latent, so it should
be "integrated out" :-)
- maybe it shouldn't, because z[i] could actually transfer
information between y[i,j] of the same site i. For example, when
y[i,1] = 1, the model will immediatelly know z[i] = 1 without
question, so this could somehow influence the inference for nodes
y[i,2], y[i,3] etc... But maybe this will not influence the overall
result at all (?)

Thanks a lot! Have a beautiful Christmass time :-)

Tomas

messages.author: 247b990d236a7af6
messages.subject: Re: occupancy model: does leaving out a latent variable (hierarchy level) result in an equivalent model?
parts:
You've left out a whether y[i,1] and y[i,2] are independent or not.  They are not independent so your revised model is currently incomplete.

Jim

messages.author: 39971e2c19b8ec70
messages.subject: Re: occupancy model: does leaving out a latent variable (hierarchy level) result in an equivalent model?
parts:
Wow, this is really surprising!

Thanks Andrew and Jim for responses. I looked more deeply at the
likelihood function, and interestingly, I came to the opposite
conclusion: that the simple model (without the latent variable) is
equivalent to the first one!!

I'd be grateful if you checked it, I could have made some mistake
there? https://stats.stackexchange.com/a/442009/5509

It expands on Andrews explanation on conditional probabilites, but
more formally.

Tomas

On Sun, 22 Dec 2019 at 16:36, <cro...@ualberta.ca> wrote:
>
> My non-technical answer is that the reason you need z[i] (where z[i] is 1 or 0) is that the probability of detecting the species during the survey is a conditional probability. What this means is that there are 2 possibilities: 1) the species exists at the site, in which case the probability of detection is p; or 2) the species does not exist at the site, in which case the probability of detection is 0. The model is estimating p independent of pi. This is what allows it to differentiate between probability of occupancy and probability of detection. Thus, if the species was detected at least once at the site, then z[i] will be 1 in every iteration and the model is able to estimate p independently, and then apply p to the sites where the species wasn’t detected to estimate a probability of occupancy that is independent of probability of detection.
>
>
>
> If the model is written as: y[i,j] ~ dbern(pi[i] * p[i,j]), then it cannot make these independent estimates, and occupancy estimates are biased low because they are confounded with probability of detection. This give biased parameter estimates as well.
>
>
>
> Clear as mud?
>
>
>

messages.author: 247b990d236a7af6
messages.subject: Re: occupancy model: does leaving out a latent variable (hierarchy level) result in an equivalent model?
parts:
Your model is still incomplete. Consider the likelihood that y11=0 and y12=0. That likelihood is 1−π1+π1(1−p11)(1−p12)=1−p11π1−p12π1+p11p12π1. If you multiply the associated two likelihoods that you present in CrossValidated, you don't get that result. How does your description obtain the correct result?  Answer:  It doesn't address that.  Again, your approach to avoid a mention of a latent variable is not necessarily wrong. It is just incomplete.  

What you need to do is show the likelihood for the resulting visit status for all visits at a single site rather than just for a particular visit at a particular site.  (Then one makes the assumption of independence of sites.)

Jim

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: occupancy model: does leaving out a latent variable (hierarchy level) result in an equivalent model?
parts:
A good way to look at this is by the marginal probability of y[i, 1:J] (data from J visits to site i).

This is written out in the second answer of the StackExchange thread you linked.  This shows that if J = 1, the marginal probabilities are equivalent, but for J > 1, they are not.  That makes sense.  For J = 1, detection probability and occupancy probability are not identifiable (setting aside single-visit occupancy ideas that bring in covariates and rely on parametric assumptions and are not the point here).  For J > 1, the probability mass function for the vector random variable y[i, 1:J] is not the same for the two models, so the models are not equivalent.

I'm confused by seeing that the StackExchange answer concludes (correctly) that the models are not the same, but I think you are saying it concludes they are the same?  Maybe there was some asynchrony in what was written when?

-Perry
